transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-18
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ruiz (CISO, NovumGen), Samir Khan (Head of Platform), Priya Mehta (Legal), Ike Turner (SRE)
Links shared: https://redwood.app/security-pack/novumgen , https://drive.example.com/novumgen-kms-diagram (placeholder)

Summary: quick Q&A focused on contractual wording for 'no training' on customer data, how keys are handled for encryption, whether prompts are persisted, and what audit trails are available. Customer wants explicit SLA commitments and a short technical follow-up for SREs.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan): all right hello everyone thanks for joining, uh we're Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Maya and Liam from our eng team. how's everyone doing?
00:14 Speaker 2 (Elena): good thanks, real quick we wanted to make sure this call focuses on two things: the legal wording around "no training" and the KMS details for bring your own key. we've got legal and platform on the line.
00:30 Speaker 1 (Jordan): perfect. that's the agenda. quick run through of our SOC 2 and ISO posture then how we handle prompt retention, then deep dive KMS.
00:45 Speaker 3 (Maya): hi all, i'll start with the high level. Redwood does not use customer prompt/content for training unless explicit opt-in is given. in hosted mode we default to ephemeral prompts for API calls flagged as sensitive, we also have a no-train flag on requests.
01:12 Speaker 4 (Samir): can you clarify what you mean by "ephemeral prompts"? like they're not written to disk or are they encrypted at rest?
01:26 Speaker 3 (Maya): yeah sorry, ephemeral means we keep minimal KV cache for the session in memory and we don't persist prompts to long-term storage when the no-train flag is set. ephemeral still uses disk-backed caches for inference efficiency in some dedicated flows but those are encrypted and rotated, and not retained for training.
01:50 Speaker 2 (Elena): and where are those caches located regionally, we need EU residency for certain data types.
02:03 Speaker 3 (Maya): region pinning is supported — you can route to eu-west-1 or a Private deployment in your VPC. for hosted accounts we have region tenancy options and we can provide a dedicated cluster for residency requirements.
02:25 Speaker 4 (Priya): legal wants the exact clause language. 'No training on customer data' is different from 'no retention' — we need to ask that it's contractually forbidden to use any PII/PHI as training data in any future model updates.
02:45 Speaker 1 (Jordan): understood. we have a standard no-train clause we can propose; i'll share wording after this call. quick note: we also provide audit logs and object-level retention controls to prove data wasn't used.
03:05 Speaker 3 (Maya): regarding audit logs, we capture request metadata, token counts, model variant used, timestamps, and KMS key IDs if BYOK is enabled. logs are stored per retention policy and can be exported to your SIEM.
03:30 Speaker 5 (Ike): what about encrypted logs — are the logs themselves encrypted with our key or Redwood's?
03:40 Speaker 3 (Maya): if you enable BYOK, we can tie log encryption to your KMS key for object-level logs; otherwise logs are encrypted with Redwood-managed keys. we can also stream logs to your cloud account so keys are in your boundary.
03:58 Speaker 4 (Priya): ok that addresses a lot. but we need an assurance that transcripts/prompts containing PHI are never used. does Redwood have a runtime flag at the API layer to opt-out?
04:12 Speaker 3 (Maya): yes, there's a request header and SDK option: training_control: "no_train". when set, requests are excluded from any data collection pipeline used for model updates. that's our primary technical control.
04:30 Speaker 1 (Jordan): addition from a contractual point: we'll include a no-train appendix that references the header and says that any request marked no_train will not be used for model training.
04:48 Speaker 2 (Elena): can that be extended to system transcripts? sometimes we ingest call transcripts for embeddings; we want a global account-level setting.
05:00 Speaker 3 (Maya): yes, account-level default no-train is available. you can enforce at the tenant level so every request inherits the flag unless explicitly overridden.
05:16 Speaker 4 (Samir): on bring-your-own-key — how does Redwood handle the KMS lifecycle? do we manage any plaintext, or is the key only used in the HSM?
05:27 Speaker 3 (Maya): good question. with BYOK we never receive your plaintext key. you rotate keys in your KMS; Redwood holds only the key reference and uses KMS API calls to encrypt/decrypt. for certain Private deployments we can integrate via direct HSM peering.
05:50 Speaker 5 (Ike): what's the canonical diagram of that flow? we want to see where tokenization happens, where KV cache is encrypted, etc.
06:00 Speaker 3 (Maya): i'll upload a KMS architecture diagram after the call. it'll show envelope encryption: data encrypted with a locally generated data key, that key encrypted with your KMS key, and only the encrypted data key is stored with Redwood.
06:20 Speaker 2 (Elena): does Redwood support HSM-backed keys from cloud providers and on-prem HSMs?
06:28 Speaker 3 (Maya): yes — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and external HSMs via PKCS#11 for Private deployments.
06:40 Speaker 1 (Jordan): quick interjection, a lot of customers also ask about RBAC and SSO — Priya maybe you want to hear that angle?
06:48 Speaker 4 (Priya): yes please. we need SSO + enforced RBAC so only certain groups can change retention windows or turn off no-train.
07:00 Speaker 3 (Maya): Redwood supports SAML SSO, OIDC, and SCIM for provisioning. role-based policies are configurable at the org and project levels. audit logs capture who changed settings and when.
07:20 Speaker 5 (Ike): can we lock the no-train flag via policy so only security admins can toggle it?
07:28 Speaker 3 (Maya): yep, we support policy enforcement — you can create a permission group that disallows toggling data governance flags.
07:38 Speaker 2 (Elena): legal: what about downstream model vendors? if Redwood upgrades the underlying model to a new open model, is there any chance that customer data previously marked no-train leaks into the next model because of internal fine-tuning?
07:55 Speaker 1 (Jordan): policy-wise we separate production telemetry from any model training datasets. no-train flagged data is quarantined from training pipelines. we also have evaluation sandboxes where data used for evals is synthetic or customer-provided opt-in only.
08:20 Speaker 4 (Priya): we will want that in the MSA and likely a right-to-audit clause.
08:28 Speaker 1 (Jordan): understood. we've had customers include right-to-audit clauses and we are open to SOC 2 Type II evidence and providing remediation plans if gaps are found.
08:40 Speaker 3 (Maya): small caveat: for hosted models we sometimes run infrastructure upgrades that require short-term logs for debugging; those are ephemeral and encrypted and we can narrow retention windows contractually.
09:05 Speaker 4 (Samir): how long are request logs kept by default?
09:11 Speaker 3 (Maya): default 90 days for request metadata; full transcript retention is 30 days by default in hosted, but we can set to 0 for ephemeral-only or stream to your account instantaneously.
09:28 Speaker 5 (Ike): 30 days is too long for PHI. we want immediate forward-only to our S3 bucket and zero retention in Redwood.
09:36 Speaker 1 (Jordan): that's doable — we have log forwarding and can set per-tenant retention to zero, effectively making Redwood a pass-through for your sensitive content.
09:48 Speaker 2 (Elena): can you give a concrete policy name or API call to enable that?
09:54 Speaker 3 (Maya): yes, policy: data_retention.mode = "forward-only" and storage.destination = "s3://novumgen-logs". i'll include the exact API snippet in the follow-up doc.
10:10 Speaker 4 (Priya): switching to encryption, is there support for encrypting in transit and at rest?
10:18 Speaker 3 (Maya): TLS 1.3 in transit, and at-rest encryption via envelope encryption with either Redwood-managed keys or BYOK.
10:28 Speaker 5 (Ike): curious about key rotation — if we rotate keys in our KMS, does Redwood rewrap data keys automatically?
10:36 Speaker 3 (Maya): yes, we support seamless key rotation. the data key is re-encrypted with the new KMS key reference as part of a background job; we keep previous keys for decryption of older objects per retention policy.
10:50 Speaker 4 (Samir): ok let's talk audit logs again — what fields are in the logs and do they include request bodies?
11:00 Speaker 3 (Maya): logs include request id, user id, org id, model variant, token counts, timestamps, and KMS key id reference; request bodies are not logged by default when no-train is set, but metadata is. we can provide redaction policies for logs to strip PII.
11:25 Speaker 2 (Elena): can you show a sample log line?
11:30 Speaker 3 (Maya): sample: {timestamp, request_id, org_id, user_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, kms_key_id, action}. i'll paste a sanitized example in the follow-up.
11:48 Speaker 4 (Priya): legal follow-up — we need to confirm whether Redwood ever uses data for internal model tuning for metrics like latency improvement even if no-train is set.
12:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan): we do collect aggregate telemetry for performance but it's pseudonymized and does not include prompt content or PII when no-train is set. we can add contractual language to prohibit even pseudonymized usage if required.
12:20 Speaker 2 (Elena): what about backups? if data is in a backup snapshot, is that excluded from training?
12:28 Speaker 3 (Maya): backups are encrypted and subject to the same retention/ no-train filters. we exclude no-train flagged content from backup datasets used for training. backups retained for disaster recovery are kept per agreed policies and can be rotated or purged on demand.
12:50 Speaker 5 (Ike): we need to test the end-to-end flow — send a test request with PHI, ensure it forwards to our S3 and Redwood has zero retention. can we schedule that?
13:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan): absolutely — that's part of the technical deep dive. propose a 60-min slot with DevOps and SREs to run through the BYOK and forward-only retention test.
13:15 Speaker 4 (Samir): competitor question — do you allow customers to use local models on-prem and have Redwood orchestrate inference?
13:24 Speaker 3 (Maya): Redwood Private supports integrating with on-prem model runners; we can orchestrate and provide the same API surface while keeping data local. that's often the path for highly regulated PHI workloads.
13:40 Speaker 2 (Elena): in that case do you still provide audit logs to our central SIEM?
13:46 Speaker 3 (Maya): yes, logs can be exported to your SIEM endpoint even for Private deployments.
13:55 Speaker 4 (Priya): legal again — we might request a bespoke clause that forbids use of any customer-delivered data in any internal benchmark datasets now or in future. can Redwood commit to that?
14:10 Speaker 1 (Jordan): we can draft contract language; we'd want to align legal teams, but we have customers with similar clauses. we'll send reference language.
14:25 Speaker 5 (Ike): about RBAC, can RBAC integrate with our existing groups in Okta?
14:32 Speaker 3 (Maya): yes, via SCIM provisioning we sync groups and roles; mapping policies can limit who can access audit logs or flip retention settings.
14:44 Speaker 2 (Elena): switching to incident response — if there is suspected leakage, what's Redwood's playbook?
14:55 Speaker 1 (Jordan): we have an IR runbook that includes notification timelines, root cause analysis, forensic artifacts, and a remediation plan. for enterprise we offer a dedicated escalation path and optional SLA credits.
15:15 Speaker 4 (Priya): would you provide the IR runbook redacted for our review?
15:22 Speaker 1 (Jordan): yes we'll include that in the security pack link.
15:30 Speaker 3 (Maya): small note on tokenization and PHI — if you prefer, we can run a preprocessing step to detect and redact PHI on ingress before it's ever persisted or sent to models. that's configurable.
15:48 Speaker 5 (Ike): what's the false positive rate on that redaction? we need to avoid breaking downstream NER tasks.
15:58 Speaker 3 (Maya): it's tunable — we can run it in audit-only mode first so you can review redactions, then flip to block mode.
16:12 Speaker 4 (Samir): ok outstanding items — Jordan to send SOC2, Maya to send KMS diagram and API snippets, Priya to review clause.
16:25 Speaker 1 (Jordan): yes will do.

(Crosstalk/overlap)
16:35 Speaker 2 (Elena): thank you all — one last question: is there any case where Redwood would resale our data or provide it to a third party?
16:45 Speaker 1 (Jordan): no, Redwood's data use policy prohibits resale. that's in our privacy policy and contract. we'll include explicit language.
16:55 Speaker 4 (Priya): legal to legal: we'll review and propose edits.
17:05 Speaker 1 (Jordan): good, next step — schedule the KMS deep dive. will you send times?
17:12 Speaker 4 (Samir): yes we'll propose tomorrow 10am or Thursday 3pm.
17:20 Speaker 3 (Maya): perfect.

(End of substantive discussion, rest of meeting administrative wrap-up)
17:40 Speaker 1 (Jordan): recap: share SOC 2/ISO artifacts, provide KMS diagram and API sample, draft no-train clause, set up BYOK + forward-only test with SREs, and provide IR runbook.
17:58 Speaker 2 (Elena): thanks.
18:05 Speaker 1 (Jordan): thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and CRM. bye.

Notes on transcription quality: medium — some proper nouns and acronyms may be mis-transcribed (e.g., PKCS#11 as 'P-K-C-S eleven' in the raw export), timestamps approximate.
